audit: scripts/selftest-other-reasons.sh:104-105 (ARM 6) asserts rc==0 AND zero FAIL-prefixed stdout lines on the clean path — the invariant is pinned where the output is produced. The verifier builds rc and report in a single branch (_verify returns (1, fail-text) or (0, OK-text); no path emits FAIL-text with rc 0).
question: Nothing covers verifier-prints-rc0-while-output-says-failed. Reachable, or contract-forbidden?
revisit_trigger: ARM 6 removed or weakened in the verifier selftest, OR a real observed incident of FAIL-text with rc 0. Either way the fix belongs in the verifier and its selftest — never a stage-90 arm. A stub-based stage arm would test invented stub behavior, and the only stage-side 'handling' (grepping verifier output for FAIL) is output-sniffing, forbidden by R12 ('Do not grep for the line you expect').
ruling: REFUSE the arm. Three independent bars, all met: (1) unreachable by construction — single-branch rc/report pairing, no divergent path exists to arm; (2) already pinned one layer down (ARM 6), the correct home for an output-discipline invariant; (3) no honest stage behavior exists for the hypothetical — the stage cannot distinguish lie from truth without sniffing output. An arm for an impossible state is the decoration this lane keeps deleting.
